page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Becquerel
lines: Becquerel (Bq): the activity of a radioactive
sample in which one nucleus disintegrates per
It is the SI unit of activity.
steps.margin_note: First mark. One disintegration per second, and the words "SI unit of activity".
steps.why: Activity is a rate of decay, not an amount of material, so its unit counts disintegrations per second and nothing else.
common_mistakes: Defining becquerel as a number of nuclei. It is a rate of disintegration.

recall.must_convey: That one becquerel is an activity of one disintegration per second, and it is the SI unit of activity.
accept: one becquerel is one decay per second
reject: three point seven into ten power ten

steps.memory_tip: Bq is the smallest possible activity: one decay, one second.

steps.label: Curie
lines: Curie (Ci): the activity of a radioactive
per second is called one curie.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The number 3.7 × 10¹⁰ and the relation to the becquerel.
steps.why: The curie was fixed as the activity of one gram of radium-226, which is why the number is an awkward 3.7 × 10¹⁰ rather than a round power of ten.
common_mistakes: Saying curie is an SI unit. Becquerel is the SI unit; curie is the older one.

recall.must_convey: That one curie is an activity of 3.7 × 10¹⁰ disintegrations per second, that is 3.7 × 10¹⁰ becquerel.
accept: three point seven into ten power ten disintegrations per second
one curie is three point seven into ten to the ten becquerel

steps.memory_tip: One gram of radium was the original curie — hence the odd 3.7 × 10¹⁰.

insider_note: Both units are defined by a number of disintegrations per second. Write the number, the unit and the relation 1 Ci = 3.7 × 10¹⁰ Bq.
